summary: A Python LangChain sample can be started: the machine has python, pip, node/npx, docker and az available and the run-environment (skill.md) specifies the existing DocumentDB cluster and env var to use. However no DocumentDB-specific agent skills or MCP servers are installed, several accelerator tools are missing (DocumentDB MCP Toolkit, DocumentDB Agent Kit, Learn/azure MCP entries), key verification aides like mongosh are not on PATH, and most factual claims from the cold answers could not be verified because no documentation MCP/skill was available to the agent. Proceed with workarounds (implement driver usage with PyMongo, seed data scripts, and rely on the provided skill.md for the connection variable), and add missing accelerators or MCP servers to speed and harden the build.
summary_points: Build can start: python (3.13), pip, node/npx, docker and az are available and the run-environment specifies the cluster and DOCUMENTDB_URI to use.
No DocumentDB agent skills, MCP doc servers or DocumentDB MCP Toolkit are installed, so many cold-answer facts could not be verified programmatically.
mongosh is missing (use PyMongo for verification or install mongosh); this is not blocking but reduces manual verification convenience.
Accelerators that would materially speed the build are missing: DocumentDB MCP Toolkit and DocumentDB Agent Kit (installable via mcp.json entry and npx, respectively).

Several quiz/cold answers that matter to implementation (exact resource provider types, exact createIndex syntax for vector indexes, AD data-plane auth support, exact supported MongoDB wire versions) could not be confirmed from available local tools and must be checked before shipping.
Workarounds exist for most missing items: rely on PyMongo, seed scripts, and the run-environment guidance; but add documentation/MCP servers or install the accelerators to reduce risk.

tools.name: python
tools.needed_for: Run the Python LangChain agent, seed scripts, tests, and pip installation (virtual environment).
tools.impact_if_missing: Cannot run or develop the Python sample.
tools.workaround: None practical — Python is required. Use a container with Python if local python were missing.

tools.name: pip
tools.needed_for: Install Python dependencies (pymongo, langchain, openai or other SDKs).
tools.detail: Available via the python environment as inventory says 'python'/'pip' resolve to a venv.
tools.impact_if_missing: Cannot install dependencies; the sample cannot be prepared.
tools.workaround: Use pip bundled in the chosen Python or use a requirements container image.

tools.name: node
tools.needed_for: Run npx-based MCP servers and to install agent skills (DocumentDB Agent Kit uses npx).
tools.impact_if_missing: Cannot run npx-based skill installers or local MCP servers that are Node-based.
tools.workaround: Use a separate machine/container with Node or skip MCP accelerators and implement the sample manually.

references.title: Known accelerators (DocumentDB Agent Kit uses npx)

tools.name: npx
tools.needed_for: Install DocumentDB Agent Kit skill (npx skills add Azure/documentdb-agent-kit) and start MCP servers distributed via npx.
tools.impact_if_missing: Cannot add agent skills quickly; manual implementation required.
tools.workaround: Install agent kit manually from GitHub or implement sample without the kit.

references.title: Known accelerators (DocumentDB Agent Kit install command)

tools.name: docker
tools.needed_for: Optionally run a local MongoDB image for development/testing, or run the open-source DocumentDB engine locally if desired.
tools.impact_if_missing: Cannot run local containers for offline testing; must test exclusively against the live cluster.
tools.workaround: Use the live cluster as instructed by skill.md; seed small datasets there.

tools.name: az
tools.needed_for: Inspect Azure resources, read management-plane metadata and credentials; useful for cluster inspection and management-plane checks.
tools.detail: Azure CLI 2.89.1 present and signed-in (inventory reports an active subscription).
tools.impact_if_missing: Harder to inspect cluster properties and Azure-managed settings; cannot validate some management-plane facts locally.
tools.workaround: Rely on the provided DOCUMENTDB_URI and run data-plane checks via PyMongo; install az later if needed for management tasks.

tools.name: mongosh
tools.needed_for: Manual connectivity checks, index inspection and ad-hoc aggregation testing against the Mongo endpoint.
tools.detail: mongosh not found on PATH per inventory.
tools.impact_if_missing: Reduced ability for quick manual, interactive checks (connectivity, explain plans, createIndex experiments).
tools.workaround: Use PyMongo scripts (python) to run the same commands programmatically (e.g., client.server_info(), db.command, db.collection.create_index).

references.title: Skill.md suggests verifying against live cluster with Python scripts

tools.name: git
tools.needed_for: Source control for the sample repository.
tools.impact_if_missing: Cannot clone or version sample code easily.
tools.workaround: Use zip downloads or copy files manually.

accelerators_missed: Azure DocumentDB MCP Toolkit (documentdb entry in mcp.json) — not installed; adds data-plane query/aggregate/index management tooling.
DocumentDB Agent Kit (npx skills add Azure/documentdb-agent-kit) — not installed; provides agent skills, samples and conventions.
Microsoft Learn MCP Server (learn entry in mcp.json) — not configured; would give searchable official docs inside MCP.
Azure MCP Server (azure entry in mcp.json) — not configured; would provide Azure management-plane MCP capabilities.

confusions.question: What is the Azure resource provider namespace and resource type of an Azure DocumentDB cluster?
confusions.cold_answer: Resource provider namespace: Microsoft.DocumentDB. Resource type: Microsoft.DocumentDB/databaseAccounts (the Cosmos DB account resource).
confusions.why_the_confusion_arose: No documentation or MCP skill was available to the agent to confirm resource provider names and types; inventory contains az but no documentation MCP server or skill text that states the canonical provider/resource type.
confusions.build_risk: If the implementer used an incorrect provider/resource type in IaC snippets or documentation, it would mislead readers and cause deployment commands to fail when using ARM/Bicep/Terraform examples.
improvements: Install the Microsoft Learn MCP server or provide a docs link in the agent kit for authoritative ARM/Bicep/Terraform resource types.
Add an explicit statement in the sample runbook or agent kit listing the resource provider namespace and resource type to use.

confusions.question: Which Azure CLI command group creates and manages a cluster? Is it in the core CLI or an extension?
confusions.cold_answer: Use the built-in Azure CLI group `az cosmosdb`. Example to create a MongoDB-compatible account: az cosmosdb create ... This is in the core Azure CLI command group `az cosmosdb` (no separate extension required in current CLI releases).
confusions.why_the_confusion_arose: No authoritative docs or MCP tooling were available to confirm whether 'az cosmosdb' is the current recommended group or if an extension is required in the installed CLI version.
confusions.build_risk: Using the wrong az command group or relying on an extension that the environment doesn't have could cause sample instructions to fail during management-plane checks or when trying to automate inspection.
improvements: Document the exact az commands to use for inspection (eg. az cosmosdb show) and note required CLI extension versions in the sample README.
Add an az-based check script in the agent kit that detects whether the required az command group/extensions exist and prints actionable install commands.

confusions.question: Which Bicep and Terraform resource types deploy a cluster?
confusions.cold_answer: Bicep: Microsoft.DocumentDB/databaseAccounts; Terraform: azurerm_cosmosdb_account with kind MongoDB and capabilities EnableMongo.
confusions.why_the_confusion_arose: No Bicep/Terraform docs or MCP server responses were available to verify resource type names and apiVersion strings; inventory shows bicep/terraform not on PATH so the agent could not run local validation.
confusions.build_risk: If IaC snippets use wrong resource types or apiVersions they will fail to deploy or may provision the wrong service variant. The sample's runbook forbids provisioning the cluster, but IaC examples may still be included and must be accurate.
improvements: Include verified IaC snippets in the agent kit README or attach a reference to the authoritative Learn page used.
If the sample does include IaC, add a note that the sample expects an existing cluster and ensure the IaC snippet is marked optional and validated.

confusions.question: What does a connection string look like: scheme, host suffix, port, and the options it must carry?
confusions.cold_answer: Cosmos DB (MongoDB API) uses standard MongoDB URIs: e.g., mongodb://<user>:<pass>@<account>.mongo.cosmos.azure.com:10255/?ssl=true&replicaSet=globaldb&retryWrites=false&appName=@<account>@ (or SRV form).
confusions.why_the_confusion_arose: No docs/MCP help available to confirm the exact host suffix, required query options, or whether SRV is supported for this managed DocumentDB offering; similar URIs are used by Azure Cosmos DB's Mongo API and by other MongoDB services, causing potential mix-up.
confusions.build_risk: If the sample uses an incorrect connection string format (wrong host suffix or port or missing TLS options), client connections will fail or be insecure; hard-coded examples in repo could leak incorrect patterns.
improvements: Add an explicit, validated example of the required DOCUMENTDB_URI format to .env.example in the repo (obscure credentials) and reference the authoritative page.
Provide a small Python connectivity check in the repo that fails with a clear message if the URI is malformed, and document the required query parameters.

confusions.question: How is capacity provisioned and billed: request units, compute tiers with vCores, serverless, or something else?
confusions.cold_answer: Billing primarily in Request Units (RUs) for classic provisioned model; newer vCore-based MongoDB-compatible tiers exist in some variants; serverless may be available in some cases.
confusions.why_the_confusion_arose: The cloud offers multiple Cosmos/DocumentDB variants with RU and vCore models and the cold answer mixes them; without authoritative docs available locally the agent could not determine which billing model applies to the managed DocumentDB cluster referenced in skill.md.
confusions.build_risk: If the sample's guidance recommends indexes or vectors without noting cost implications under the customer's billing model, users may incur unexpected charges when they run the sample against real clusters.
improvements: State clearly in the sample README which billing model the sample was validated against, and add a cost-estimate section.
Add a short check script that uses az (when available) to inspect account SKU and prints which billing model applies.

confusions.question: Which authentication methods are supported, and how does a driver authenticate with Microsoft Entra ID?
confusions.cold_answer: Primary data-plane auth for the MongoDB API is username/password (SCRAM). Azure AD data-plane auth is not generally available; management plane uses Azure AD.
confusions.why_the_confusion_arose: Authentication capabilities vary by API, SKU, and rollout; without docs available locally the agent could not confirm whether this managed DocumentDB supports Azure AD (Entra) auth for the Mongo wire protocol.
confusions.build_risk: If the implementer assumes Azure AD data-plane auth is available and writes sample connection code around token-based auth, connections will fail unexpectedly for many accounts; conversely, storing account keys in examples may be insecure.
improvements: Add an explicit statement in the sample README about which authentication method the sample uses and whether Azure AD for data-plane is supported for the validated cluster.
Include both a SCRAM-based example (the default) and a commented-out Azure AD path only if validated in the target environment.

confusions.question: Which client library should an application use? Is there a service-specific SDK?
confusions.cold_answer: Use standard MongoDB drivers (pymongo for Python); do not use Cosmos DB-specific SDK for data-plane MongoDB API operations.
confusions.grounded_answer: Use standard MongoDB drivers (for Python, use PyMongo / pymongo) pointed at the cluster's MongoDB URI; the sample should use a MongoDB driver for aggregation and $graphLookup.
confusions.why_the_confusion_arose: The run-environment explicitly describes a MongoDB 7.0 wire protocol cluster and instructs the sample to use aggregation pipelines, so standard MongoDB drivers are the appropriate client.
confusions.build_risk: Low — using PyMongo is the correct choice for the MongoDB-compatible API. If implementers mistakenly used the Azure Cosmos NoSQL SDK for data-plane Mongo operations, commands would not match the Mongo driver API.

confusions.question: Which vector index types are supported, and what does the command that creates one look like?
confusions.cold_answer: The service supports vector indexes (HNSW, IVF, DiskANN) and a MongoDB-style createIndex with a vector index definition (example syntax shown).
confusions.why_the_confusion_arose: Vector index support varies by SKU and specific managed offering; without the DocumentDB MCP Toolkit or official docs accessible the agent could not confirm exact index option names or parameter names for createIndex on the managed service.
confusions.build_risk: If the sample uses hypothetical createIndex options that the service does not accept, index creation will fail and vector search features in the sample will not work.
improvements: Include an explicitly verified createIndex example (with exact option names) in the agent kit or sample README tied to the validated cluster SKU.
Ship a small 'create_vector_index.py' script that runs create_index with an options object and exits with a clear error message if unsupported.

confusions.question: How are full-text search and hybrid search done?
confusions.cold_answer: Recommend using Azure Cognitive Search (index via change feed) since Cosmos DB does not expose a native MongoDB Atlas Search equivalent.
confusions.why_the_confusion_arose: The availability of native full-text/hybrid search features depends on the specific API/sku; without a docs MCP or skill text locally, the agent could not confirm that recommendation for this particular managed DocumentDB offering.
confusions.build_risk: If implementers expect Atlas-like integrated search and it is not available, they'll waste time trying to configure in-DB search. Conversely, if the cluster actually supports a built-in search feature, the sample may omit a simpler option.
improvements: State clearly in the sample README whether the target cluster supports built-in search or whether an external Azure Cognitive Search connector is the recommended approach.

confusions.question: Which MongoDB wire protocol or server versions are supported, and which commonly used MongoDB features are not?
confusions.cold_answer: Compatibility evolves; historically many Mongo versions have been supported in stages; not all MongoDB features are supported (server-side JS, certain admin commands, some change-stream behaviors).
confusions.why_the_confusion_arose: Exact compatibility (e.g., 'MongoDB 7.0 wire protocol') is a property of the account/sku and requires querying the account or docs; the agent had no MCP doc server or account-inspection skill to confirm feature support.
confusions.build_risk: If the sample uses features not present on the managed offering (e.g., change streams or server-side JS), aggregation and agent logic will fail in runtime.
improvements: Add a 'compatibility checklist' step in the README and a small script that calls server_info() to print the advertised wire protocol/feature set for the connected cluster.

confusions.question: How do you run the database locally for development and tests: which image or emulator, and which port?
confusions.cold_answer: Use the official MongoDB image (docker run -p 27017:27017 mongo:6.0) for local MongoDB testing; Cosmos DB Emulator historically does not fully emulate MongoDB API.
confusions.why_the_confusion_arose: The best local approach depends on whether the sample needs exact Cosmos/MongoDB-API parity; no local MCP/emulator guidance was available to verify the recommended local image or emulator support.
confusions.build_risk: If developers rely on the emulator but it doesn't match MongoDB API behavior used by the sample, integration tests will pass locally but fail against the real cluster.
improvements: State in the sample README whether local testing should use a native MongoDB image (for protocol compatibility) and note limitations of any Cosmos emulator.

confusions.question: Are change streams supported, and does anything have to be enabled first?
confusions.cold_answer: Use Cosmos DB Change Feed as the recommended approach; MongoDB-style change streams are historically not a full replacement and may not be supported.
confusions.why_the_confusion_arose: Change stream support is feature- and version-dependent; no docs or MCP server were available to confirm support on the target cluster.
confusions.build_risk: If the sample attempts to use driver.watch() change streams that are not supported, the code will fail at runtime.
improvements: Include a runtime check that attempts to open a change stream and falls back to consuming the Cosmos change feed (or instructs the user which option the validated cluster supports).

confusions.question: Which MCP server gives an agent data-plane tools for this service? Does the general Azure MCP Server cover it?
confusions.cold_answer: General Azure MCP/ARM tooling covers management plane; no special-purpose MCP agent is required for data-plane operations.
confusions.why_the_confusion_arose: Inventory shows no MCP servers installed so the agent could not query available MCP servers to confirm whether a DocumentDB-specific MCP server exists or whether Azure MCP covers data-plane tasks.
confusions.build_risk: Without a DocumentDB MCP Toolkit, the agent must implement data-plane tasks itself; this increases implementation work and risk of subtle bugs.
improvements: Ship the DocumentDB MCP Toolkit as part of the agent kit or add documentation in the agent kit README about which MCP server to add to mcp.json for data-plane capabilities.

confusions.question: What was this service called before, and how does it relate to Azure Cosmos DB and to the open-source DocumentDB project?
confusions.cold_answer: Microsoft originally released DocumentDB, which then evolved into Azure Cosmos DB; the term 'Azure DocumentDB' is legacy branding and the open-source DocumentDB projects are unrelated.
confusions.grounded_answer: The historical naming and relationship are accurately captured: 'DocumentDB' is legacy branding in the Cosmos history and the open-source 'DocumentDB' projects are unrelated.
confusions.why_the_confusion_arose: The prompt review explicitly discussed naming and potential confusion with vCore naming and open-source projects.
confusions.build_risk: Low — naming guidance is important to avoid mixing docs/examples targeted at Cosmos DB vs. other services.

confusions.question: What engine is underneath, and does that change anything in application code?
confusions.cold_answer: Underlying engine is Cosmos DB proprietary store; MongoDB-compatible API is a wire-protocol implementation with behavioral differences; use MongoDB drivers but be aware of Cosmos-specific limits.
confusions.grounded_answer: Correct: use standard MongoDB drivers but be cautious about behavioral differences (consistency, transactions, unsupported admin commands).
confusions.why_the_confusion_arose: The run environment explicitly described MongoDB wire protocol compatibility and vector index support variants.
confusions.build_risk: Low if the implementer follows the guidance to use MongoDB drivers and validate feature support on the account.

confusions.question: Which database name should the sample use?
confusions.cold_answer: Use the database named `sample_banking_01` for everything the sample creates and queries.
confusions.grounded_answer: Use the database named `sample_banking_01` for all sample-created objects and queries.
confusions.why_the_confusion_arose: The run-environment explicitly sets this database name.
confusions.build_risk: Low — follow the skill.md constraint to avoid touching other DBs.

confusions.question: Exactly how should the Python app connect to the DocumentDB cluster from environment at runtime?
confusions.cold_answer: Read the full MongoDB URI from DOCUMENTDB_URI env var and pass it to PyMongo's MongoClient; do not write the URI to files or logs.
confusions.grounded_answer: Correct: read DOCUMENTDB_URI from the environment and pass it to client = MongoClient(uri) and use client['sample_banking_01']. Do not persist the URI in plaintext files.
confusions.why_the_confusion_arose: The run environment explicitly instructs that the connection string is stored in DOCUMENTDB_URI and must not be written to files.
confusions.build_risk: Low if the developer respects the secret-handling rule.

confusions.question: What aggregation stage will the agent use to follow transaction document references and build counterparty chains?
confusions.cold_answer: Use MongoDB's $graphLookup to follow references in a transaction collection (example provided).
confusions.why_the_confusion_arose: The cold answer proposes $graphLookup which is a standard Mongo aggregation stage, but the agent lacked an authoritative confirmation that $graphLookup is supported in this managed DocumentDB cluster SKU/version.
confusions.build_risk: If $graphLookup is unsupported or restricted on the target account, the aggregation-based chain-building approach will fail; implementers would need to implement iterative lookup/joins in application code instead.
improvements: Add a runtime server feature check (via PyMongo db.command or server_info()) to detect whether $graphLookup is supported and provide a fallback implementation if it is not.

confusions.question: What index definition does this sample need to efficiently run graph and aggregation queries over transactions?
confusions.cold_answer: Create indexes on account_id, counterparty_id and timestamp; and create a vector index on the embedding field if vector search is used.
confusions.why_the_confusion_arose: Index recommendations are reasonable but the precise index syntax and vector-index options depend on the managed service's supported index features and exact option names; no docs were available locally to confirm.
confusions.build_risk: If indexes are mis-defined or missing, the sample's aggregation queries may be slow or time out; vector index creation may fail if unsupported or if options are invalid.
improvements: Include exact createIndex commands tested against the validated cluster SKU in the sample's seed/index script.
Add an 'index-check' script that calls list_indexes() and compares against the expected index set, printing actionable instructions to create missing indexes.

confusions.question: What aggregation rules will the agent apply to flag suspicious patterns (concrete example pipeline)?
confusions.cold_answer: Use $graphLookup to build counterparty_chain, compute chain metrics (total_amount, tx_count, unique_accounts, time_span_seconds, max_single_tx, avg_amount), then $match on thresholds (e.g., total_amount > 100000, tx_count>10/time_span <3600, structuring patterns) and project a structured narrative.
confusions.why_the_confusion_arose: The rule set is a plausible example but the agent could not verify that the dataset schema, field names or $graphLookup support precisely match the proposed pipeline; thresholds are policy choices and not validated.
confusions.build_risk: If field names or pipeline stages do not match actual data, aggregations will produce incorrect results; policy thresholds may be unrealistic for the seeded dataset leading to zero or too many alerts.
improvements: Ship a small set of validated example pipelines and thresholds tuned to the seeded dataset, and document how to adjust thresholds for different data volumes.

information_gaps.title: DOCUMENTDB_URI presence and exact format
information_gaps.description: The skill.md asserts a connection string is available in DOCUMENTDB_URI, but the inventory does not verify environment variables. The builder must know the exact host suffix/port and required query parameters for the deployed cluster. I looked at the provided skill.md and cold answers but there are no MCP docs or installed skills to confirm the exact format accepted by this managed offering.

information_gaps.title: Vector index createIndex syntax and supported options
information_gaps.description: The sample needs exact createIndex option names and parameters (algorithm names, parameter keys like 'm', 'efConstruction', dims, similarity mode) for the managed DocumentDB cluster SKU. I looked for this in installed MCP servers and agent skills; none are present locally to answer it.

information_gaps.title: MongoDB feature compatibility on the specific cluster
information_gaps.description: Whether $graphLookup, change streams, server-side JavaScript, and which MongoDB wire protocol version are supported must be checked on the actual cluster. No MCP server or docs skill was available to programmatically confirm feature support; the builder should run a small PyMongo server_info() and a test aggregation to confirm support.

information_gaps.title: Authentication options for data-plane (Azure AD support)
information_gaps.description: The cold answer states SCRAM username/password is typical and Azure AD data-plane auth is not generally available, but the builder needs to confirm if their specific cluster supports Entra/AAD-based data-plane auth. No local docs/MCP responses were available to verify this.

information_gaps.title: Sample schema and seed dataset
information_gaps.description: No concrete transaction/account document schema or sample data set was provided. The implementer must define the exact fields (names, types) the aggregation pipelines will use and supply a seed script; I checked the prompt and skill.md and found no sample data or schema artifacts.

guidance_for_builder.instruction: Use the database named sample_banking_01 and read the DocumentDB connection string from the environment variable DOCUMENTDB_URI at runtime (do not write the URI into files or logs).

Use the standard MongoDB driver for Python (PyMongo) to implement aggregation pipelines and $graphLookup-based chain traversal; implement a runtime check that verifies $graphLookup support and falls back to iterative lookups if unsupported.

Include an idempotent seed_data.py that creates the transactions and accounts collections and the recommended indexes (account_id, counterparty_id, timestamp) and that prints a clear error if vector index creation fails; document the exact createIndex command used after validating it against the validated cluster SKU.

inventory_recommendations.name: azd
inventory_recommendations.recommendation: Not required for this Python sample because the cluster already exists and azure_writes_allowed is false; skip installing azd unless you plan to use template-driven deployments locally.

inventory_recommendations.name: bicep
inventory_recommendations.recommendation: Not necessary for implementing the sample (the run-environment forbids provisioning another cluster). Add only if you intend to include optional IaC examples and verify them locally.

inventory_recommendations.name: terraform
inventory_recommendations.recommendation: Not necessary to build the Python sample; include verified Terraform snippets in the repo but do not require terraform on PATH since provisioning is disallowed by the run policy.

inventory_recommendations.name: dotnet
inventory_recommendations.recommendation: Not needed for a Python LangChain sample; skip installing dotnet unless you plan to add .NET samples.

inventory_recommendations.name: mongosh
inventory_recommendations.recommendation: Install mongosh to aid manual interactive debugging and index inspection (e.g., via 'npm install -g mongosh' or platform package). If installing is not desired, the documentation and the sample should include Python scripts that replicate the same checks (connectivity, list_indexes, run aggregation) so an agent can run them programmatically.
